# Read-only Android Automotive telemetry. Any addition requires security review.
android.car.permission.CAR_SPEED
android.car.permission.CAR_ENERGY
android.car.permission.CAR_EXTERIOR_ENVIRONMENT
android.car.permission.CONTROL_CAR_CLIMATE
android.car.permission.CAR_VENDOR_EXTENSION
# Trip recording outlives the dashboard, which on API 26+ requires a foreground service.
# Install-time permissions, no vehicle access, no network.
android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE
android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE
# Reviewed and approved 2026-09-04 (CP-043), NOT YET DECLARED in any manifest.
# Approval and declaration are different statements: this file says a permission passed
# security review, the manifest says the shipped APK asks for it. These three land with
# CP-042, in the same commit as the code that uses them, and not before.
# Route requests to a driver-configured routing host. https and a host allowlist on the
# initial URL and every redirect hop. Origin, destination and profile leave the car;
# nothing else ever does. See analysis/CP-043_network_and_location.md.
android.permission.INTERNET
# Route origin and altitude. Runtime request from a parked screen the driver reaches,
# never at start and never from a service; refusal falls back to the CP-040 route source
# with the forecast intact. Coarse location is insufficient: it snaps origins to the wrong
# side of a junction and carries no usable altitude.
android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
# Only if a service ever reads position while backgrounded. Nothing does today. The
# foreground type mask stays derived from permissions held at runtime, never from the
# manifest.
android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION
